messages:
alex_sales: FYI  MedLedger procurement just sent back their SIG and called out in-flight KV replication between AZs. They want customer-managed HSM keys and HSM attestation for any replicated state. Theyre holding the POC until we provide either HSM attestation or a vendor risk acceptance. Can we triage?

maya_sec: Thanks Alex. Do we have the exact CAIQ line?

alex_sales: Quote: 'Does the vendor support customer-controlled, hardware-backed key management (HSM) and cryptographic attestation for any replicated or cached model state transmitted between availability zones? If not, provide compensating controls and vendor-signed risk acceptance.'

liam_infra: Short answer: hosted mode uses provider-managed KMS for ephemeral replication traffic; we do not expose customer HSM for in-flight RAM or network-level replication. Dedicated/Private can bind to customer KMS/HSM for persisted storage and some replication paths.

zoe_se: Proposed customer-facing reply draft: "Redwoods hosted inference uses transient, in-memory replication for availability; while hosted does not currently expose hardware-backed attestation for in-flight memory replication, Redwood provides customer-managed encryption for persisted artifacts, strong isolation between tenants, short TTLs on replicated state, and enhanced auditability. Dedicated/private deployments are available for customers requiring HSM-backed attestation."

maya_sec: Internal compensating controls (draft):
```
- Ephemeral-only replication: no replication writes to disk; replication kept in RAM and GCd on session end.
- Minimize replication window: default replication TTL = 30s, configurable to 10s.
- Replay protection + mTLS enforced for replication channels.
- CMEK for any persisted artifacts (logs/traces/checkpoints) with customer-provided key options.
- Immutable, signed audit trail for replication events; retention 18 months.
- Continuous integrity checks and anomaly detection on replication endpoints; immediate revocation path if anomalies detected.
- Manual attestation package (signed runtime snapshot + logs) available on request until automated attestation is implemented (~8 weeks ETA).
```

maya_sec: Residual risk assessment: "elevated" for regulated healthcare customers due to lack of HSM attestation for in-flight memory; "moderate" otherwise. CISO sign-off required for vendor risk acceptance.

rachel_legal: For the signed risk acceptance we need scope, controls list, residual risk statement, signatory list (sec lead + CISO), and a non-promissory clause about future features. Keep external language plain and non-technical.

liam_infra: Feasibility: all compensating controls are implementable short-term except automated attestation. Manual attestation package = 4 business days first delivery, subsequent on-demand packages 1-2 days. Automation ~8 weeks.

ciso: I can provisionally approve an exception for the POC with MedLedger provided: (1) compensating controls are implemented and documented, (2) legal signs off on the external wording, and (3) we maintain a remediation plan to deliver automated attestation within the stated ETA. I will review the internal memo today.

alex_sales: Customer wants this by EOD tomorrow. Maya/Rachel/Zoe can we get a short internal memo + the customer paragraph? Ill ask procurement to pause gating if we have vendor-signed acceptance.

zoe_se: I dropped a concise customer paragraph below for review: "Hosted Redwood inference leverages transient, in-memory replication for high availability. While hardware-backed attestation for in-flight replication is not available in hosted mode, Redwood enforces strict isolation, short replication windows, customer-managed encryption for persisted artifacts, and enhanced auditability. For customers requiring hardware-backed attestation, Redwood can provide Dedicated/private deployment options."

rachel_legal: Edits applied: remove "not available" phrasing to soften: "Hosted Redwood inference leverages transient, in-memory replication for high availability. Hardware-backed attestation for in-flight replication is currently provided via Dedicated/private deployments; for hosted deployments, Redwood enforces strict isolation, short replication windows, customer-managed encryption for persisted artifacts, and enhanced auditability. An approved vendor risk acceptance can be provided for POC deployments."

maya_sec: I'll create SEC-2120 and attach the compensating controls checklist + residual risk assessment. Reviewers: maya_sec, rachel_legal, ciso. Please confirm and Ill route for signature.

tickets-bot: SEC-2120 created: https://redwood.internal/tickets/SEC-2120 (assignees: maya_sec, rachel_legal, ciso).

alex_sales: Thanks everyone. Tagging @ciso @rachel_legal @maya_sec @liam_infra. Ill hold MedLedger until the signed memo is uploaded. :pray:
